idee_recherchee.texte: Quantum mechanics and general relativity are fundamentally incompatible, and the search for a theory of quantum gravity, such as string theory or loop quantum gravity, tries to unify the physics of the very small with the physics of the very large.

titre_video: Scientists Are Freaking Out Over Space Time (It's Not Real)
titre: Le paradoxe de l'information des trous noirs
resume: Quantum mechanics holds that information cannot be destroyed, but anything falling into a black hole seems to lose its information forever. This information paradox implies either quantum mechanics is wrong, our understanding of black holes is incomplete, or reality works in ways we cannot comprehend.
texte: Ironically, getting [music] sucked in is where black holes seem to break physics in the most fundamental way possible. Quantum mechanics has one [music] absolute rule, information cannot be created nor destroyed. The quantum state of every particle, every interaction, every moment of history [music] must be preserved somehow, somewhere. But, black holes seem to violate this rule completely. When something falls into a black hole, all information about it appears to be erased forever. This creates [music] what physicists call the information paradox. Either quantum mechanics is wrong, or our understanding of black [music] holes is incomplete, or reality itself works in ways we can't comprehend. And all three are more than plausible.
